model_annotation: The bar chart displays the effect sizes of various linguistic models across different language families and isolated languages, with error bars indicating variability. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by language family, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," quantifies the magnitude of the effect, ranging from 0 to 30. Each category on the horizontal axis contains a group of bars, each representing a different model: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red). The legend in the upper right corner identifies each model by its corresponding color. The chart shows that the effect sizes vary significantly across models and language families, with the IE-Indic family showing the highest effects for most models, particularly for XLM-B2, which reaches over 20. In contrast, the Isolate category shows very low effects for all models, generally close to zero. The Semitic family also shows high effects for XLM-B2, exceeding 20, while other models have lower values. The Uralic family shows a mix of low and moderate effects across the models. The error bars suggest that the variability in effect size is also considerable, especially for the IE-Germanic and IE-Indic families.
